title: Smooth Adjacent Pairs
description: Return a new List of averages of adjacent integers using Java truncation toward zero. Input is nonempty; do not modify it. This mirrors HW01–03 smooth.
hints: You need one output entry per adjacent pair.
Use a long sum before division to avoid overflow.
explanation: Scan consecutive pairs once, compute each average using a long intermediate to avoid overflow, and append to a new list. A list of length one produces no pair.

title: Safe Java Integer Average
description: Implement the exact mathematical (a+b)/2 truncated toward zero, without int overflow. The returned value always fits int. HW04 explicitly tests MIN/MAX boundaries. You may use long here; the homework requires int-only, covered separately in review.
hints: Cast before adding, not afterward.
Java integer division truncates toward zero.
explanation: Promote both operands before adding: ((long)a + b) / 2. Converting after adding would preserve an already-overflowed int.

title: Sequence Palindrome
description: Return true if an integer sequence reads identically forward and backward. Do not mutate the input. Based on Lab01.
hints: Compare symmetric index pairs.
explanation: Compare mirrored positions moving inwards. Stop on the first mismatch; the empty and singleton sequences are palindromes.

title: Queue Front with Restoration
description: Return the first element of an ArrayDeque without modifying its abstract contents. Queue is nonempty; use removal/append/rotation instead of peek() to simulate layering.
hints: Save the first value, then rotate the Queue until the original order returns.
explanation: Temporarily remove the first queue entry and rotate the remaining entries before restoring the original front at the end. The outgoing queue must be unchanged.

title: Shift Boundary Between Two Stacks
description: Model HW07 Sequence on Stack: left is stored with its top at the end (ArrayDeque.peekLast()); right has its front at the top (ArrayDeque.peekLast()). Shift top elements to make left size k while preserving rev(left)*right in the course model.
signature: void shiftBoundary(ArrayDeque<Integer> left, ArrayDeque<Integer> right, int k)
hints: The operation is always a pop from one stack and push to the other.
explanation: Move one element between the two stacks to change the boundary while preserving their combined logical sequence. Handle empty-side preconditions.

title: Queue Set: Add Unique
description: Simulate a Set layered over a Queue. Add x to queue only if not already present. Preserve relative order of existing entries.
hints: Sets cannot contain duplicate values.
explanation: Test membership before enqueuing into the underlying queue. Rotate to preserve existing order; adding duplicates must not increase the set size.

title: Map Move-to-Front
description: Given a LinkedList of keys that are unique, move a matching key to the front. If absent, preserve the original list. This adapts HW09 moveToFront for Map.Pair keys.
hints: Find matching key and preserve all other entries.
explanation: Search for the requested key and move the matching entry to the front while retaining every other entry. Be careful not to lose the pair during rebuilding.

title: Mathematical Modulo
description: Return mathematical a mod b in [0,b), given b>0. Java remainder may be negative; this is directly based on HW10 and your P03 code.
hints: Compute remainder and adjust when negative.
explanation: The Java remainder operator can yield a negative result; normalize the remainder into [0,n). Assumes positive modulus n.

title: Hash Bucket Index
description: For a key hashCode and capacity>0, return a valid bucket index. Do not use Math.abs(hash) because MIN_VALUE is problematic.
hints: A bucket index must be nonnegative and less than capacity.
explanation: Obtain the key’s hashCode and apply nonnegative modulo to the bucket count. Do not use Math.abs, which fails on Integer.MIN_VALUE.

title: Hash-Table Bucket Histogram
description: For each integer x, use mathematical x mod capacity as its bucket. Return an int[] of bucket counts. Mirrors HW10 hash-distribution exercise.
hints: Create capacity counters initialized to zero.
Every key maps through mathematical modulo.
explanation: Initialize one counter per bucket; calculate the index for each key and increment that counter. The sum must equal the number of entries.

title: Word Frequency Map
description: Count case-insensitive words separated by any nonletter characters. Return a Map from lowercase word to count. Inspired by the uploaded WordCounter project.
hints: Normalize the case before using the map.
Split into word tokens; skip empty tokens.
explanation: Normalize tokens into a common case, ignore separators, and count occurrences by key. Test repeated and mixed-case words.

title: Sorted Word Count Lines
description: Produce sorted lines "word:count" for a frequency Map, one line per word (no trailing newline), sorted case-insensitively. Adapts the WordCounter HTML table pipeline.
hints: Collect map keys into a list before sorting.
explanation: Sort the collected map keys before output rather than relying on the map iteration order; keep counts associated with their own keys.

title: NaturalNumber Multiply By Ten
description: Representation is a String where zero is "" and all other values have no leading zero. Return the updated representation after multiplyBy10(k), 0<=k<=9.
hints: Zero must remain canonically represented.
explanation: For the canonical decimal representation, append the new digit to nonzero numbers. Zero needs special treatment to avoid leading zeros.

title: NaturalNumber Divide By Ten
description: Given canonical NaturalNumber representation rep, return a 2-element List<String>: updated rep and decimal digit removed. For empty rep, result is ["", "0"].
hints: Remove exactly the last digit.
explanation: Remove the final digit and return it; the remaining prefix is the updated natural number. A single-digit number becomes canonical zero.

title: Canonical Decimal String
description: Normalize a nonempty decimal-digit string by deleting leading zeroes. Represent zero with the empty string, as in NaturalNumber3.
hints: Find first nonzero digit.
explanation: Remove redundant leading zeros while preserving the distinguished representation of zero. Each nonzero string must begin with a nonzero digit.

title: Size of a BinaryTree
description: Given a CourseSupport.Node<Integer> binary tree (null means empty), count nodes recursively. This mirrors HW12/HW21 and preserves the input naturally.
hints: Empty tree is base case.
Count root plus both subtrees.
explanation: Use the empty-tree base case 0; otherwise return 1 plus the sizes of the two subtrees. Restore the source tree if its API transfers children.

title: Height of a BinaryTree
description: Return height in nodes: empty tree has height 0, and a leaf has height 1.
hints: Height depends on longest child path.
explanation: Use 0 for an empty tree; otherwise take 1 plus the greater of the two child heights. The recurrence differs from node count.

title: Maximum Label in Tree
description: For a nonempty binary tree, return its largest integer label using recursion. Unlike a BST, no ordering is assumed.
hints: Check root and every nonempty subtree.
explanation: Start with the current root, compute maxima of each nonempty child recursively, and return the greatest. Respect the nonempty input requirement.

title: BinaryTree Prefix Representation
description: Return HW13 prefix representation: empty tree "()", otherwise root + "(" + left representation + right representation + ")".
hints: Use a recursive helper for both subtrees.
explanation: Represent an empty tree by (), otherwise emit root(leftRepresentation rightRepresentation). Preserve the exact nested parentheses.

title: Deep-Copy a BinaryTree
description: Return a fresh, structurally equal tree with no shared nodes. Input is unchanged. Based on HW13 BinaryTree copy.
hints: Allocate a new node for each existing node.
explanation: Construct a fresh tree with a copied root and recursively copied children. Mutating or reusing input nodes violates deep-copy expectations.

title: BST Membership
description: Return whether x occurs in an integer BST. Search only the relevant branch at each step. This mirrors HW14 and P04.
hints: Compare x with root and choose only one subtree.
explanation: Compare the target with the root; recurse into only the relevant subtree, not both. Equality is the success case.

title: BST Insert Unique
description: Insert x into a BST if absent. Return root; maintain BST and avoid duplicates. Nodes are mutable.
hints: Root empty creates new node.
Duplicates are not inserted in this version.
explanation: Descend until reaching an empty child position, following the comparator. For a unique-key BST, do not insert a duplicate.

title: Smallest Node in BST
description: Return the minimum integer in a nonempty BST. This is the value used as inorder successor during removal.
hints: Keep following left children.
explanation: The minimum is found by following left links until no left child remains. An empty input is outside the contract.

title: BST Remove a Label
description: Remove x from a unique-key BST, if present. If a node has two children, use the smallest label in its right subtree as replacement.
hints: Solve zero- and one-child cases before two-child case.
For two children, copy successor label then remove successor from right subtree.
explanation: Search for the target, handle zero/one-child removal directly, and for two children replace with the smallest right-subtree label and remove it there.

title: Insert into a Sorted Queue
description: Given sorted integers in a mutable ArrayDeque, insert x while preserving ascending order. Simulates HW15 insertInOrder using a temporary queue.
hints: Move values that precede x to a temporary queue.
explanation: Copy already-sorted entries into a temporary queue until the insertion point, add x, then append the rest. The comparator determines order.

title: Insertion Sort a Queue
description: Sort an ArrayDeque<Integer> ascending using insertion sort behavior: extract one entry at a time and insert into the correct location of a temporary sorted deque.
hints: Build a sorted output by repeatedly inserting extracted values.
explanation: Maintain a separate sorted queue; repeatedly remove an entry from the input and insert it at its proper position in the sorted queue.

title: Partition a Queue
description: Return two Lists [front,back], putting input values <= pivot in front and > pivot in back while preserving relative order. Mirrors HW16 partition.
hints: Partition condition is <= pivot, not < pivot.
explanation: Compare each entry against the pivot and move it into the ≤ or > partition. Preserve all elements and handle duplicates consistently.

title: Recursive Quicksort
description: Return a new ascending-sorted List using a recursive quicksort with the first element as pivot; do not modify input.
hints: Pick pivot, partition remaining, recursively sort partitions.
explanation: Choose a pivot, partition the remaining entries, recursively sort both partitions, and recombine left + pivot + right. Length 0 or 1 is the base case.

title: Sift Down Min-Heap
description: Fix the min-heap ordering starting at index i in array a where both child subtrees are already valid min-heaps. Active entries are indices 0..size-1. Modify in place.
hints: Compare both children and select smaller.
Continue from the child index after swapping.
explanation: At each step compare the current item with the smaller child; swap only if the heap order is violated. Continue until ordered or at a leaf.

title: Build a Min-Heap
description: Convert an int[] into a valid min-heap in place. Use bottom-up heapify; any valid heap is accepted. Must preserve input multiset.
hints: Start at last parent floor(n/2)-1.
Sift each internal node down.
explanation: Heapify by sifting down internal nodes from the last parent to the root. Verify the resulting array satisfies all parent-child comparisons.

title: Remove Minimum from Heap
description: Given a nonempty valid min-heap int[], return the minimum. The input array may be mutated. Return value only; caller assumes the last element becomes inactive. Implement root removal and siftDown on active prefix.
hints: Store the root before replacing it with the last active entry.
explanation: Save the minimum root, replace it with the last active item, decrease size, and sift down. Edge cases include size 0 and 1.

title: Check Heap Ordering (Any Shape)
description: Return true iff every parent <= its children in a binary tree. Do not require complete shape. This is specifically HW17 satisfiesHeapOrdering.
hints: Only compare each parent and direct children; recurse.
Do not test completeness here.
explanation: Recursively check the root against each present child and check each child subtree. Shape completeness is intentionally not required here.

title: Check Complete Binary Tree
description: Return true iff a binary tree has complete-tree shape (all levels full except possibly last, last filled left to right). Any labels permitted.
hints: Breadth-first traversal: after the first missing child, no real node may appear.
explanation: A complete tree fills levels left-to-right. During breadth-first traversal, once a missing child appears, no later node may have a child.

title: SortingMachine: Extract k Minima
description: Given integer list (duplicates retained) and k between 0 and size, return the k smallest elements in ascending order using PriorityQueue rather than sorting the full collection.
hints: A min-heap naturally returns the smallest active entry.
explanation: Use the heap to extract the minimum k times while retaining duplicates. The extracted list is sorted ascending and the remaining heap stays valid.

title: Singly Linked Stack Push
description: Given CourseSupport.LinkedStack with top, length, and LNode fields, push x in O(1). Directly adapts HW18 Stack2.
hints: Prepend new node at head.
explanation: Link the new node to the previous top, then update top. This is constant time and does not touch the remaining chain.

title: Singly Linked Stack Pop
description: Remove and return the top value from a nonempty CourseSupport.LinkedStack in O(1). Update length and top pointer.
hints: The top node contains the item to return.
explanation: Save the old top value, advance the top pointer, and decrement size. The removed node becomes unreachable from the stack.

title: Reverse-Queue Enqueue with Sentinels
description: Implement enqueue at the abstract rear of CourseSupport.ReverseQueue, whose real nodes are stored backward between preFront and postRear. Maintain both prev and next pointers and length.
hints: New abstract rear belongs immediately after preFront.
Four pointer assignments are needed.
explanation: Insert the new rear entry immediately after preFront because the physical node order is reversed. Reconnect next and prev in both directions.

title: Reverse-Queue Dequeue with Sentinels
description: Implement dequeue at abstract front of CourseSupport.ReverseQueue; real nodes are stored backward between preFront and postRear. Queue is nonempty.
hints: Front is postRear.prev.
Bypass the node in both directions.
explanation: Read front from postRear.prev; unlink it by connecting its predecessor directly to postRear, then decrement length.

title: List Cursor Retreat
description: Given CourseSupport.CursorList with left/right ArrayLists storing cursor partitions, move the last element from left to the front of right. Left nonempty. Mirrors HW19/P06 retreat semantics.
hints: The combined list must remain unchanged.
explanation: Move the left/right boundary one entry toward the start without changing concatenated contents. An empty left half is invalid.

title: List Cursor Advance
description: Given CourseSupport.CursorList, move first right element to the end of left. Right nonempty. This is the inverse of retreat.
hints: Maintain left*right concatenation.
explanation: Advance the boundary one entry toward the finish, transferring the right-front value to left-end. The total sequence stays fixed.

title: Count CALLs in Statement AST
description: Given a simplified CourseSupport.SNode AST with kinds BLOCK/IF/IF_ELSE/WHILE/CALL, count all CALL nodes recursively, including custom names. Original AST is unchanged.
hints: Base leaf counts one if CALL; otherwise recurse children.
explanation: Traverse the AST by kind: recurse through BLOCK/IF/IF_ELSE/WHILE, count calls at CALL leaves, and reconstruct transferred nodes.

title: Count Primitive Calls in AST
description: Count only primitive BL calls among move, turnleft, turnright, infect, skip, and turnback. Custom calls do not count. Use CourseSupport.SNode.
hints: A CALL is not necessarily a primitive instruction.
explanation: Only primitive instruction CALLs contribute. User-defined instruction names may need different handling; follow the task’s primitive set.

title: Count skip Calls in AST
description: Return the number of CALL("skip") nodes in a simplified AST, preserving its value. Mirrors practice exam extra Q18.
hints: Only a CALL whose name equals skip contributes one.
explanation: Count one for CALL(skip), recurse over every branch and loop body, and restore the original tree. This counts syntax, not runtime executions.

title: Rename Calls in AST
description: Mutate an AST by changing every CALL whose name equals oldName to newName. Other kinds and conditions remain unchanged. Mirrors HW25 renameInstruction.
hints: Apply to matching CALL leaf and traverse all child subtrees.
explanation: At a CALL leaf compare the name with oldName and replace it if equal; recursively process all subtree kinds and preserve original structure.

title: Pretty Print a BL Statement
description: Render simplified BL AST using two spaces per nesting level. BLOCK emits children; CALL emits its name; WHILE emits "WHILE condition DO", its body, then "END WHILE". Other kinds are not tested.
hints: BLOCK does not print an opening/closing line.
Indent the WHILE body by 2 spaces.
explanation: Indent children at offset + INDENT_SIZE, print matching IF/ELSE/WHILE boundaries, and reassemble each Statement after recursive printing.

title: Count Skip Calls in Program
description: A CourseSupport.BProgram has context Map<String,SNode> and a main body SNode. Count CALL skip occurrences in both. This is practice exam extra Q19.
hints: Do not forget instructions defined in the context.
explanation: Sum skip calls over every definition in the context and the main body, using the Statement helper. Swap both pieces back to preserve the Program.

title: Rename a Program Definition and Calls
description: Mutate BProgram: rename a user-defined instruction key oldName to newName and every matching CALL in all definitions and main body. Assume newName is not already a context key.
hints: Rename the definition key, every definition body, and the main body.
explanation: Remove/reinsert the renamed definition under its new key, traverse the remaining definition bodies, and rename calls in the main body.

title: Next Word or Separator
description: Given text, starting index and separator string, return the longest contiguous substring where every character has the same separator membership as the first character. Based on HW26 and WordCounter.
hints: Remember whether the starting character is a separator.
explanation: Classify the starting character as whitespace or word, then scan a maximal contiguous run of the same type.

title: Tokenizer with END_OF_INPUT
description: Tokenize a String by whitespace only (space, tab, newline, carriage return), discard whitespace and append a literal END_OF_INPUT final token. Based directly on HW26.
hints: Whitespace is the separator category here; punctuation stays within words.
Always append END_OF_INPUT once.
explanation: Process lines into maximal tokens, keep the non-whitespace ones in order, then append exactly one END_OF_INPUT sentinel.

title: Recursive Descent Arithmetic
description: Evaluate a valid expression containing nonnegative integers, +,-,*,/, parentheses (int division truncates toward zero) and no whitespace. Mirrors HW28 five-method grammar. Implement by your own parser.
hints: Break parsing into expr, term and factor for precedence.
Maintain one source cursor shared by all parser methods.
explanation: Implement grammar levels as functions: expr handles +/−, term handles ×/÷, factor handles parentheses, digit-seq reads numbers. Recursion enforces precedence.

title: Validate Signed Real Constants
description: Return whether a string matches HW27 signed-real-const grammar: optional + or -; decimal digits before dot; fractional digits optional; optional E exponent with optional sign and at least one digit. Requires a dot.
hints: The decimal point is mandatory under this specific grammar.
Exponent starts with uppercase E.
explanation: Match the optional leading sign, numeric forms and optional exponent according to the homework grammar. Reject malformed exponent or decimal forms.

title: Map Buckets with Collisions
description: Create n bucket lists and insert keys into buckets by Math.floorMod(key.hashCode(),n). Return bucket lists in bucket-index order; preserve insertion order within each bucket. Simulates Map4 array-of-buckets representation.
hints: All buckets must exist, including empty buckets.
explanation: Store colliding keys in the same bucket, using key equality for lookups and removal. A collision never means the keys are equal.

title: Validate Heap and Shape
description: Given an arbitrary binary tree, return true only if it satisfies BOTH min-heap ordering and complete binary-tree shape. HW17 separates these conditions.
hints: Combine breadth-first completeness with parent/child order checks.
explanation: Test order and completeness separately. Both must hold for a valid min-heap; local ordering alone is not sufficient.

title: Summarize Program AST Structure
description: Return a Map counting every AST node kind (BLOCK, IF, IF_ELSE, WHILE, CALL) in Program body plus all context definitions. The Program and nodes must be unchanged.
hints: Count the node itself, then all descendants.
explanation: Traverse the Program AST and collect the requested structural summary without mutating the components. Every kind has different child counts.

title: BST Inorder Traversal
description: Given a BST, return a sorted ascending List of all its node labels using recursion. Do not modify tree.
hints: Left, root, right gives BST sorted order.
explanation: Inorder traversal visits left, root, right. In a BST this produces values in sorted order (subject to the task’s duplicate convention).

title: Rehashing Map Entries
description: Given Map<String,Integer> and bucketCount>0, return Map<Integer,List<String>> of keys grouped by nonnegative bucket index. Include empty buckets, and sort each bucket’s keys for deterministic output.
hints: Every key belongs in exactly one initialized bucket.
explanation: Allocate the new buckets and redistribute every old entry using the new capacity. Recompute indices; simply copying buckets is incorrect.

title: Queue Reversal Using a Stack
description: Reverse ArrayDeque<Integer> in place by using a stack (another Deque). Covers layered queue/stack algorithms from HW06–08.
hints: Stack is last-in-first-out; Queue is first-in-first-out.
explanation: Push dequeued elements onto a stack then pop back into the queue. LIFO reversal yields the reversed FIFO ordering.
